title: Quality Assessment of Videos about Radiotherapy-Related Oral Mucositis on YouTube in Brazil
screen_reason: Cross-sectional analysis of 104 eligible YouTube Brazil videos on radiotherapy-related oral mucositis. Although the overall grading (poor/fair/good) is a quality scheme, the 'poor' category is defined purely by veracity - a video scoring 1 ('totally wrong') or 2 ('partially wrong') on at least one of six pre-defined content variables - and the authors report it as the share containing misinformation (10.6%, n = 11). That is a CONTENT share of items judged inaccurate against expert reference definitions.

estimates.date: searched and downloaded 21 September 2024; content evaluated October-November 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of YouTube videos on radiotherapy-related oral mucositis containing incorrect information (classified 'poor')
estimates.denominator: 104 videos analysed, from the first 200 retrieved for the Portuguese search term 'boca ferida radioterapia' after excluding videos under 1 min (n = 5), over 15 min (n = 39) and off-topic (n = 52)
estimates.definition: Video scored 1 ('The information is totally wrong') or 2 ('The information is partially wrong') on at least one of six a priori content variables (definitions of head and neck cancer, radiotherapy and mucositis; frequency; signs and symptoms; prevention/treatment)
estimates.misinfo_def: Group 1 - incorrect information (scores 1-2) ... (1) The information is totally wrong; (2) The information is partially wrong
estimates.source_quote: Eleven videos (10.6%) were classified as ‘poor’ because they contained at least one incorrect information. ... Overall, 10.6% (n = 11) were classified as ‘poor’ due to the presence of misinformation.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Six content variables with reference definitions set a priori by a panel of three dentists specialised in cancer care from the current scientific literature; two independent evaluators scored every included video offline after a two-stage calibration, a senior investigator resolved non-consensus; inter-rater agreement Cohen's kappa > 0.8.
estimates.moderator_quote: A YouTube Brazil search (www.youtube.com.br) was conducted using the term “boca ferida radioterapia” (“mouth sore radiotherapy”), applying only the default relevance filter. ... The first 200 videos were selected, but only those lasting 1-15 min were included ... Videos unrelated to the topic were also excluded.
estimates.notes: Single keyword, relevance-ranked first 200 videos, hence denom_selection=curated. The 'fair' (32.7%) and 'good' (56.7%) categories are completeness/comprehensiveness grades, not veracity, and were not extracted. Per-variable incorrect-information shares in Table 2 (head and neck cancer definition 7/104 = 6.7%; mucositis definition 2 = 1.9%; signs and symptoms 1 = 1.0%; prevention and treatment 2 = 1.9%; radiotherapy definition and frequency of mucositis both 0) are the components of this composite, not separate estimates. Minor internal inconsistency between text (51.0%/85.6%/54.4% physicians/lay-public/likes) and Table 1 (50.9%/85.5%/54.3%) does not touch the 11/104 cell.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: the per-variable score 1-2 shares in Table 2 (components of the composite 10.6%, not distinct estimates); the 'fair'/'good' quality grades and the information-omission shares (80.8% did not define mucositis, 92.3% did not mention frequency, etc.), which are completeness, not falsity; the discussion's comparison of the first 60 versus subsequent videos ('most were classified as good (54%), with a high percentage also being fair (42%)' vs 'satisfactory quality (59%) with fewer containing incomplete information (24%)') gives no explicit denominator and no incorrect-information share for those subsets.

rob.design: Descriptive cross-sectional video analysis; single Portuguese keyword on YouTube Brazil with default relevance filter, dedicated research account, all searches on the same day, videos downloaded 21 Sep 2024 and analysed offline; 200 screened, 104 eligible; six a priori content variables defined by three cancer-care dentists; two calibrated independent evaluators, senior investigator adjudication, Cohen's kappa > 0.8; descriptive statistics only.
rob.item6_quote: Based on the Likert scale, videos were categorized into three groups: Group 1 – incorrect information (scores 1–2), Group 2 – information not mentioned (score 3), and Group 3 – correct and comprehensive information (scores 4–5). The final classification of each video’s overall quality was determined as follows: ‘Poor’ - videos with at least one criterion scoring in Group 1
rob.item10_quote: Eleven videos (10.6%) were classified as ‘poor’ because they contained at least one incorrect information.
